subject: One-off pilot extension + credit uplift request (Nexford Health)
messages:
From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel@nextfordhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 60-day pilot extension + additional credits

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the team is excited by the latency profile and prompt routing suggestions. We made good progress with the integration, however procurement flagged two issues that will delay our signature: an internal security review (extra paperwork) and a budget cycle that doesn’t close until the end of June.

Those two items mean we won’t be able to finish the paid contract in time to use the remaining credits you provided under the standard PLG pilot window. Traffic has been strong during the trial (attached usage report), and we need another month to complete the end-to-end evaluation with our clinical QA folks.

Can Redwood consider a one-off extension (60 days) and a top-up of $25,000 in complimentary credits so we can finish validation and get an SOC2 checklist to procurement? If that’s not possible at that level, we’d accept a smaller top-up. We’re committed to a minimum committed start upon signature (TBD), but procurement needs the evaluation evidence first.

Appreciate any flexibility — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Daniel Ruiz
Director of ML Platforms
Nexford Health

Attachment: pilot-usage-20270520.csv
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: 60-day pilot extension + additional credits

Karthik / Laura — forwarding Nexford’s ask. Quick summary / my read:

- Customer: Nexford Health (DEAL-8876), enterprise healthcare prospect; strong technical fit for our routing/caching work.
- Ask: 60-day pilot extension + $25k free credits. Procurement delay + security review.
- Current usage: peak inference rates for scheduled workflows; see attached CSV.
- Upside: likelihood of a committed deal within 8–10 weeks once procurement finishes; potential for dedicated capacity order in H2.
- Risk: precedent for >PLG windows and fairly large one-off credit.

Recommendation: Approve a narrower concession to balance precedent and momentum — 45 days extension + $15k credits as one-off nonstandard concession, contingent on:
  1) Signed pilot addendum (one-page) capturing extension dates and one-time credit grant;
  2) Procurement email acknowledging plan to start committed contract after evaluation;
  3) CS to run a short health check at day 30.

Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf, pilot-usage-20270520.csv

Please advise if we should escalate to Aditya for final sign-off or if Karthik can approve at deal desk level. I’m leaning to getting Aditya on the thread if we stick with $25k.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 60-day pilot extension + additional credits

Thanks for the note and the recommendation, Irene. I agree we should be conservative but pragmatic. My take:

- Approve 45 days + $15k credits as a deal-desk one-off. This hits the middle ground and keeps momentum without a material precedent for future smaller deals.
- Require the addendum + procurement acknowledgement as you suggested.
- CS to schedule the health check; if the health check shows meaningful progress we can consider an additional 15k uplift discretionary on Aditya’s ok.

Laura — need legal to pre-clear a short addendum (one paragraph) and a template DocuSign so we can move quickly. If legal signs off, Karthik will approve the concession from deal desk.

Karthik

Appreciate the context. I reviewed the SOW-draft and proposed addendum language. Key legal/ops notes:

- We can agree to a 45 day extension and a one-time $15,000 credit grant.
- Addendum must state: credits expire at end of extension period; credits are non-transferable; extension does not change our standard trial T&Cs except as noted.
- Include a procurement acknowledgment clause (one-sentence) — customer confirms expected procurement timeline and intent to convert to a paid agreement after evaluation.
- No additional indemnities or SLA changes. If the customer insists on data residency guarantees, that will need separate escalation.

I’ll attach a clean addendum and a DocuSign-ready wrapper. If Karthik confirms, this is ready to go.
